# Meditate: full agent reference

Canonical docs: https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/
Source: https://github.com/jmcentire/meditate
Version described: 0.1.x alpha
License: MIT
Runtime: Python 3.11+

## Purpose

Meditate consolidates, compresses, and simplifies behavioral directives loaded by Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. Its target failure mode is monotonic append: after a correction, an agent adds a new exception without revising the rule that caused the failure. Contradiction is the symptom; missing replacement relations are the mechanism.

Meditate is not a generic provider-state, vector-store, workspace, tool-side-effect, or model-weight scrubber. It addresses locally inspectable instruction files and learned behavioral directives.

## Authority and temporal ordering

Authority, scope, supersession, recency, and corroboration are separate dimensions. An explicit user correction can outrank a newer assistant-authored summary. Within comparable authority and scope, newer applicable evidence is preferred, but older supporting and conflicting evidence remains in lineage. Recency is a decay weight, not an age cutoff.

Default durable evidence order:

1. Explicit user correction or reversal with an identifiable antecedent.
2. Current version-controlled instruction, qualified by scope.
3. Repeated user preference across independent sessions.
4. Deterministic outcome evidence tied to the proposed rule.
5. Active Kindex constraint, directive, or decision with provenance.
6. Agent auto-memory or summary.
7. Assistant conclusion or unverified inferred lesson.

A one-off historical imperative is session evidence, not automatically a durable global policy.

## Source and write boundaries

Configured readable sources may include Claude/Codex instruction files, prompt indexes, opt-in transcript JSONL, auto-memory, and active Kindex knowledge. History, memory, and Kindex are read-only evidence. Writable paths must be exact configured targets. Symlinked targets are refused by default.

Before a model call, evidence is streamed, deduplicated, classified, secret-scanned, locally redacted, ranked, and bounded. High-confidence secret-bearing records are excluded wholesale. Older temporal breadth is reserved during selection.

The Anthropic request contains the system prompt, constrained JSON output schema, and a canonical JSON packet. The packet includes configured target path labels and hashes; current directive IDs, headings, scopes, and locally secret-scanned/redacted text; selected evidence IDs, timestamps, source/authority/scoring metadata, and redacted text in temporal order; the authority/comparison rules; allowed targets; overlap candidates; and degradation state. It does not include unselected or wholesale-excluded history records. The transmitted material is still user-derived content and is not claimed to be anonymous or risk-free.

The model receives locally minted directive and evidence IDs and must return a total disposition: every current directive is kept, replaced, removed, or relocated exactly once. Local validation rejects unknown IDs, missing dispositions, invented quotes, unsupported destinations, unresolved conflicts, secret matches, excessive churn, source/config drift, protected-section edits, ambiguous new high-impact authority, or truncated output.

## Commands

meditate init
  Write a commented TOML configuration.

meditate inspect [--json]
  Local-only inventory and overlap candidates. No model call. No target mutation.

meditate plan [--model ID] [--effort LEVEL] [token-limit flags]
  Build a sanitized evidence packet, call the exact configured Anthropic model, validate operations, and archive a read-only proposal/report. No target mutation.

meditate apply RUN_ID --approve PLAN_SHA256
  Revalidate source/config hashes, verify the archive, bind approval to the exact plan, then replace allowlisted target files atomically.

meditate restore RUN_ID [--force] [--recover]
  Restore archived pre-images. Later hand edits block normal restore; forced restore archives diverged bytes first.

meditate run [planning flags] [--apply]
  Inspect and plan. Dry-run by default. Unattended mutation additionally requires explicit configuration, evidence allowlisting, probation, and mode gates.

meditate cron [--check] [--schedule CRON] [--apply]
  Print or validate a locked cron invocation. Never edits the crontab.

meditate purge RUN_ID [--execute] [--force]
  Preview or explicitly erase a named archive. Active recovery material requires force; erasure leaves a tombstone.

## Recovery model

Run archives use SHA-256-addressed blobs and canonical manifests under private XDG data directories. Reports and JSONL summaries live under private XDG state directories. Apply archives and verifies target pre-images before writes, uses same-directory atomic replacement, preserves modes, rechecks hashes, and rolls back changed targets on a later failure. Ambiguous recovery emits a machine-readable receipt rather than guessing.

## Privacy

Meditate has no hosted product service or CLI telemetry. `inspect` is fully local. `plan` and `run` deliberately send current directive text and selected, locally secret-scanned/redacted evidence to the explicitly selected Anthropic model. API keys are read from environment variables and never logged. See https://jmcentire.github.io/meditate/privacy.html for the complete boundary.
